newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to fire improved missiles in Gulf war games.
newsitem.headline: Iran to fire improved missiles in Gulf war games.

text.p: Iranian forces staging a major military exercise in the Gulf will fire an improved version of Chinese Silkworm missiles, Iran's official news agency IRNA reported on Monday.
It quoted navy spokesman Rear-Admiral Ashkbous Danekar as saying an updated version of the HY-2 Silkworm missile known as Piroozi (Victory)-75 would be fired later this week in the 10-day war games.
The exercises at the mouth of the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman involve some 100 ships including destroyers, gunboats, hovercraft and submarines supported by 40 fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters.

"(The missiles) are used for surface-to-surface operations as well as for ground-to-air and coast-to-sea operations," Danekar said. He did not give further details but he apparently meant that the missiles had been updated in Iran.

Navy Commander Rear-Admiral Ali Shamkhani told IRNA U.S. warships "were carefully watching the manoeuvres using their full radar, communication, and monitoring systems", but said that would not affect the war games.
Shamkhani last week condemned the presence of Western navies in the Gulf as "a kind of occupation" but said Iran's exercise "does not challenge anyone and does not signal any tension".
The United States' Fifth Fleet operates in the Gulf. British, French and other Western navies are also on patrol.
